canonical_reference: Tran, K., et al. (2024). UCCIX: Irish-eXcellence Large Language Model. University College Cork.

News content; no cultural design stated.

canonical_reference: M. N. Raihan, A. Anastasopoulos, M. Zampieri - mHumanEval: A Multilingual Benchmark to Evaluate LLMs for Code Generation - NAACL 2025 (arXiv:2410.15037)
languages: 204 natural languages (names not enumerated in accessed source)
evidence_note: Consensus of 5 independent coding rounds (majority >=3). Round A evidence: English HumanEval prompts rendered in 204 natural languages via machine translation, with expert human translations for a 15-language subset. Same programming problems across languages.

canonical_reference: Miyu Sato, Yui Obara, Nao Souma, Kimio Kuramitsu - CL-HumanEval: A Benchmark for Evaluating Cross-Lingual Transfer through Code Generation - PACLIC 2024
evidence_note: Consensus of 5 independent coding rounds (majority >=3). Round A evidence: v1 covers English and Japanese only. Docstrings regenerated in plain English then translated into Japanese with identifiers neutralised across languages; same content in both languages by design.

canonical_reference: Sumanth Doddapaneni, Mohammed Safi Ur Rahman Khan, Dilip Venkatesh, Raj Dabre, Anoop Kunchukuttan, Mitesh M. Khapra - Cross-Lingual Auto Evaluation for Assessing Multilingual LLMs - ACL 2025 (arXiv:2410.13394)
languages: Bengali; German; French; Hindi; Telugu; Urdu
evidence_note: Consensus of 5 independent coding rounds (majority >=3). Split cells: task_class 4/5. Round A evidence: YEAR filled (roster had none): arXiv Oct 2024 / ACL 2025. RECON is a human-annotated test set of 500 general-purpose instructions with human judgment scores; Section 3.1: prompts manually translated into six target languages (Bengali, German, French, Hindi, Telugu, Urdu); reference answers, instructions and rubrics remain in English. The source spans high- and low-resource languages, so no single tier. Generation purpose: benchmarking and meta-evaluation of LLM generation.

canonical_reference: Yekyung Kim, Jenna Russell, Marzena Karpinska, Mohit Iyyer - One ruler to measure them all: Benchmarking multilingual long-context language models - arXiv:2503.01996, 2025
languages: Chinese; Czech; Danish; Dutch; English; Finnish; French; German; Hindi; Hungarian; Italian; Japanese; Korean; Norwegian; Persian; Polish; Portuguese; Russian; Serbian; Sesotho; Spanish; Swahili; Swedish; Tamil; Ukrainian; Vietnamese
evidence_note: Consensus of 5 independent coding rounds (majority >=3). Split cells: data_origin 4/5; task_class 3/5. Round A evidence: Instructions and noun lists translated from English into 25 languages with native-speaker collaboration; haystack material is one non-copyrighted book natively sourced per language. Synthetic needle-in-haystack/aggregation tasks; identical content design across languages. Source splits 22 high-resource vs 4 low-resource languages (Hindi, Sesotho, Swahili, Tamil), so no single tier.

canonical_reference: Kenneth Enevoldsen, Isaac Chung, Imene Kerboua, Marton Kardos, Ashwin Mathur, David Stap, Jay Gala, Wissam Siblini, et al. - MMTEB: Massive Multilingual Text Embedding Benchmark - arXiv:2502.13595 (ICLR 2025)
evidence_note: Consensus of 5 independent coding rounds (majority >=3). Split cells: data_origin no majority ({'mixed': 2, 'native': 1}); cultural_specificity no majority ({'universal': 2}); task_class 3/5. Round A evidence: Community aggregation of 500+ quality-controlled tasks covering 250+ languages; the paper's own per-task metadata records heterogeneous production (found, created, human-translated, machine-translated, LM-generated and verified). No single tier or cultural design for the whole resource. Language count is stated as 250+, not exact, so count left empty.

evidence_note: Consensus of 5 independent coding rounds (majority >=3).
